name: In-flight aerobic and resistive exercise
description: Regular exercise on onboard devices is the main countermeasure for musculoskeletal and cardiovascular deconditioning. All astronauts exercise during missions to counteract losses in bone density, muscle strength and heart and blood-vessel performance.

name: Schedule planning and fatigue management
description: Crew schedule planning that includes circadian entrainment, work/rest assessment and protected sleep opportunities (NASA-STD-3001 [V1 6001]); sleep accommodations that limit noise and light.

name: Private medical and psychological communication
description: Routinely scheduled private medical conferences with flight surgeons and psychological support ([V1 6002], [V1 6010]); store-and-forward modes when communication is delayed.

name: Radiation shielding and sheltering
description: Vehicle shielding and designated shelter areas used during solar particle events, following mission procedures.

name: Radiation monitoring, dosimetry and alerting
description: Area and personal radiation monitoring ([V2 6161], [V2 6162]), accurate event determination and timely reporting to alert the crew; ALARA principle ([V1 4029]).

name: CO2 removal and environmental trend monitoring
description: Life-support CO2 removal, environmental monitoring and trend analysis of environmental data ([V2 6001]); habitat 1-hour average ppCO2 limited to ≤ 3 mmHg in NASA-STD-3001 V2 Rev D [V2 6004].

name: Spaceflight food system and diet
description: Planned diet and food system supporting energy, bone and overall health; intake monitoring.

name: Hydration
description: Adequate fluid intake supports kidney health; ASTRA shows hydration trends for review.

name: Infection control and environmental microbiology
description: Monitoring of microbial communities and hygiene measures in the closed habitat.

name: Periodic eye examinations and imaging
description: Clinician-directed eye examinations and imaging to detect structural changes associated with SANS.

name: Sensorimotor readaptation and task planning
description: Allowing for adaptation around gravity transitions and assessing balance and coordination before critical tasks.

name: Onboard medical capability
description: Medical kit, trained crew medical officer, medical records and approved procedures for in-mission medical care ([V1 3004]).

name: Autonomous operations and decision support
description: Onboard tools, preloaded procedures and store-and-forward communication to support crew independence as distance from Earth increases.
